items.note: Yolk-yellow header band with a sagging arc, a bold h2 title, an ink filter pill with the white dot, cream pills on their ledge, and crescent-shaded pictogram covers in category hues. All of it is clearly the reference's language. The band's art is still a disc-plus-pill stamp about 250px wide on a 1440px band, where the reference's hero art (02) is a layered scene that balances the headline.

Compact yellow band with an arcSm sag and the cluster tucked into the top corner with text kept clear. Then full-width cream filter pills with the ink selected pill and one-column cover cards. This is close to the reference phone (04) in warmth and density. The filter row scrolls off the edge, which is acceptable.

Navy page, indigo card bodies and filter pills, and a white selected pill with an ink dot. It follows the night palette of 03 convincingly, with the yellow band and saturated covers keeping their hues. It has the same small header-band stamp as the light version.

The phone night version holds together: a white cart pill, indigo filter pills and select, and the yellow band with its corner cluster. At the page foot, the footer's bottom bar turns into a bright white strip, which nothing in the reference's night palette does.

The header band correctly turns cream because a large cover follows. A crescent-shaded tote pictogram fills the hue cover, with a 32px price and the blue add-to-cart as the one conversion pill. The colour options are bordered tiles carrying arbitrary breathing glyphs (zigzag, ring, bubbles) instead of anything showing the colour, which reads generic next to the reference's purposeful rows (05).

Cream compact band with the corner cluster, and the cover directly after the title as the layout rules ask, then price, copy and a full-width blue pill. The option tiles repeat the meaningless glyphs. In one sample they wrap two-plus-one, with the radio circle sitting on the tile's edge, which is the agent's slip.

The indigo header band with its wide arc, the saturated cover and the indigo option tiles all carry the night palette well. The glyph-per-colour option tiles still say nothing about the option they label.
Solid night phone layout with the cover high on the page and a full-width blue pill. The option tiles keep their arbitrary glyphs, and the footer ends in a white bottom strip.

Well-drawn sweater pictograms with crescent shading on orange or blue covers, and a clean price-copy-action column. The size picker is the weak spot. S, M, L and XL each sit in a bordered tile with a different decorative glyph or a repeated ring, where the reference's language for picking one value is a pill row with an ink selected pill and a dot.

Good phone order: compact cream band, the cover right after the title, then price. Four full-width size tiles, each with an unrelated glyph, add bulk and noise above the primary action that a pill row would not.
The night version matches 03's navy and indigo tones, and the covers stay saturated. The size tiles carry the same decorative glyphs as in light mode.
Consistent night phone page with a white cart pill, indigo tiles and a blue add-to-cart. The size tiles with their glyphs dominate the middle of the page.

A blue header band in the cart area's hue with white on-field text, and a cream radius-xl empty panel. The panel holds a shaded basket or cart pictogram with sparkles, an h4 title, one line and an ink pill, which matches the empty-state recipe. The band's cluster is again a small stamp in a wide field of blue.

Compact blue band with the corner cluster and a tight, centred empty panel with a clear basket pictogram and an ink pill. The rhythm is close to the reference phone. The pictogram stays modest, below the spec's art size.
The blue band keeps its hue at night, with an indigo empty panel and a white pill with ink label as the night palette prescribes. The header-band art is the same undersized stamp as in light mode.
Indigo empty panel and white pill read well on navy. Below the indigo footer, the bottom bar flips to a white strip in every sample.

findings.summary: The desktop header-band art is still a 3–4 piece stamp about 230–260px wide, roughly a sixth of a 1440px band, leaving a wide empty stretch of colour between the title and the art. The reference's hero art (02) is a layered scene about as wide as the text block that balances the headline. The rc.3 recipe is unchanged: the SVG is sized by height inside a short band, so it cannot fill the trailing 40–50% the text asks for.
findings.promptFix: Size the desktop header-band cluster by width, not height. Give the art box 40–50% of the band, make the SVG `width: 100%; height: auto`, and draw it in a wide viewBox (about 400×240) holding 4–5 pieces: a lead shape, a second-hue shape cutting into it, a 48–64px star, a small sparkle and optionally a cloud at the outer edge. Let the band grow to fit the art. A cluster narrower than a third of the band reads as a sticker, not a scene.
findings.specRule: .ms-field__art > svg { height: 100%; min-height: var(--size-art); max-width: 100%; } … <svg viewBox="0 0 240 200">

findings.summary: On product detail pages, plain values such as sizes and colours are built as 2px-bordered option tiles. Each tile carries a breathing glyph that has nothing to do with its label: a zigzag for 'S', a spiral for 'XL', or the same ring or bubble pair repeated on every tile. Colour options never show the colour. The reference picks each row's glyph to mean its topic (05) and uses pill rows with the ink selected pill and a dot for picking one value. The spec sends agents here by putting glyphs on every form option tile.
findings.promptFix: A glyph goes on an option only when the option names a subject the glyph can picture. Short values such as sizes, quantities, amounts and plain variants are a segmented row of cream pills, with the selected one an ink pill with the white dot. Colour or finish options show the actual colour as a flat disc swatch with its name. Never give each value a different decorative glyph, and never repeat one glyph on every option.
findings.specRule: Where. Choice lists, navigation cards and category rows (one per row, in the row's area hue, its form chosen for the row's label); … option tiles in forms (still until hovered, focused or selected)

findings.summary: In dark mode the footer's bottom bar becomes a bright white strip under the indigo footer, a light slab at the foot of every night page that the reference's night palette never shows. The spec causes this. It builds the bar from `surface.inverse`, which flips to #ffffff at night.
findings.promptFix: The footer's bottom bar is the darkest tone of the current appearance: ink in light, the deepest navy at night. It never uses `surface.inverse`, which flips to white in dark mode.
findings.specRule: Footer | Cream band with rise arc, link columns, a signup field + ink pill; `surface.inverse` bottom bar with round icon buttons
